title: fix: guard against disposed render frames in webRequest filtering (fixes #326368)
body:
### Summary The main-process `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onBeforeRequest` filter in `app.ts` reads properties of the `WebFrameMain` (`details.frame`) that Electron hands it for each intercepted request. When the render frame backing that `WebFrameMain` has already been disposed (its webview/window was closed or navigated away) by the time the async callback runs, accessing any property throws Electron's `Render frame was disposed before WebFrameMain could be accessed`. The throw escapes into the unhandled-error telemetry pipeline. Impact: benign but noisy uncaught errors across all platforms; the request filtering for that already-gone frame is meaningless anyway. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326368 Recommended reviewer: `@deepak1556` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not definitively identified | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | — | > No single culprit commit could be confirmed. The affected functions (`isSafeFrame`, `isAllowedVsCodeFileRequest`, `isAllowedWebviewRequest`) are long-standing security filters, and the working checkout is a shallow (depth-1) clone so line-level `git blame` collapses onto the grafted HEAD and cannot attribute the originating change. Commit-message search for `isAllowedVsCodeFileRequest` / `getAllWindowsExcludingOffscreen` returned nothing (GitHub commit search only indexes messages). The `recent-regression` / `stable-anomaly` signal is most plausibly explained either by the Electron runtime bump (Electron 42, where `WebFrameMain` property access on a disposed frame throws), or by the introduction of offscreen-window filtering (`getAllWindowsExcludingOffscreen`) which made `isAllowedVsCodeFileRequest` enumerate windows and read `frame.processId`. Neither could be verified against the Step 4.0 shipped-commit ancestry gate from the available history, so no commit is named rather than guessing. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Electron as Electron webRequest participant Filter as onBeforeRequest handler participant Frame as WebFrameMain (details.frame) Electron->>Filter: onBeforeRequest(details, callback) Note over Frame: ⚠️ Root cause:
render frame already disposed
(webview/window closed or navigated) Filter->>Frame: frame.url / frame.parent / frame.processId Note over Frame: 💥 Error thrown:
Render frame was disposed before
WebFrameMain could be accessed ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts` | Crash site + fix | `isSafeFrame` L338-339 reads `frame.url` / `frame.parent`; `isAllowedVsCodeFileRequest` L359 reads `frame.processId`; `isAllowedWebviewRequest` L380 reads `frame.processId` — all on a `WebFrameMain` whose render frame may be disposed. | ### Repro Steps Hard to reproduce deterministically (timing race between frame disposal and an in-flight request). Conceptually: a webview/window that issues a `vscode-file:`, `vscode-webview:`, or `.svg` request is closed or navigated away before the main-process `onBeforeRequest` filter runs; the filter then reads a property of the now-disposed `WebFrameMain` and Electron throws. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/code/electron-main/app.ts`: add an `frame.isDestroyed()` guard before any property of the Electron-supplied `WebFrameMain` is read, at each of the three access sites in the `onBeforeRequest` filter: - `isSafeFrame`: check `frame.isDestroyed()` at the top of each loop iteration (before `frame.url` and before the loop advances via `frame.parent`) and treat a disposed frame as not safe (`return false`). - `isAllowedVsCodeFileRequest`: extend the existing null-guard to `if (!frame || frame.isDestroyed() || !this.windowsMainService)`. - `isAllowedWebviewRequest`: same extension of the existing null-guard. This is a guard clause placed *before* the throwing access (the data-producer here is Electron's own frame lifecycle — an external boundary the consumer cannot control), which is why a consumer-side guard is the correct fix rather than a producer change. It does not use `try/catch`, does not swallow anything, and preserves the existing `logService.error('Blocked ...')` telemetry calls: a disposed frame simply fails the "is this an allowed frame" check and the request is treated as not-allowed, which is the safe default the surrounding security filter already applies to unknown frames. `WebFrameMain.isDestroyed()` is the Electron-documented way to test frame liveness without triggering the disposed-access throw. **Alternatives considered:** - Wrap each access in `try/catch` returning `false` — rejected because it hides the disposed-frame condition behind exception handling instead of testing for it explicitly, and risks masking unrelated errors. ### Recommended Owner `@deepak1556` — Security Maintainer on `microsoft/vscode` (write access), owns the Electron runtime and main-process `webRequest`/security-filter area, and is actively committing (multiple commits within the last week). Passes both the team-membership and liveness gates. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29593079069) · 2.3K AIC · ⌖ 34.2 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: voice: timeout if narration audio never starts
body:
## Summary
Adds a **30-second audio-start watchdog** for solicited narration requests so voice mode recovers instead of getting stuck when the backend finishes the main LLM turn but never begins streaming narration audio.

## Behavior
- When a `request_narration` is accepted, arm a 30s watchdog that waits for the backend to start returning audio.
- **No audio within 30s** → drop the narration, release the in-flight guard, and restore voice state (re-enter the hands-free mic if enabled, else go idle / "Hold to speak…") so the user isn't stuck.
- **Audio starts** → cancel the watchdog and let the stream finalize normally via `_markNarrationHeard`. The remainder of an actively-arriving stream is **not** timed out.
- The 30s value matches the sibling `_awaitingReplyAudio` watchdog for consistency. A timeout is non-destructive: `_lastNarratedText` / the pending indicator are left untouched so the narration can be re-requested on the next focus/state event.

## Concurrency guard
Restoring state on timeout only happens when nothing else is still expected: the timed-out narration is always dropped, but the state restore is deferred while `_awaitingReplyAudio` is set or another solicited narration is still waiting for its first audio chunk. Whichever watchdog fires last performs the restore, so a narration timing out can't clobber state (or start the mic) while another response's audio is still inbound.

## Tests
Controller tests (`voiceSessionController.test.ts`) cover:
- state is restored when a solicited narration never returns audio;
- the audio-start watchdog is cancelled once audio arrives and the stream is not timed out afterward;
- restore is deferred while another solicited narration is still awaiting audio (last watchdog restores);
- restore is deferred while a direct chat reply is still awaited (`_awaitingReplyAudio`).

## Validation
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`
- `npm run precommit` (hygiene)

title: [cherry-pick] fix: restore 8 KiB Node buffer pool on linux

labels.name: cherry-pick-artifact
labels.description: Auto-generated cherry-pick PR

body:
Cherry-pick of #326334 from `release/1.129`.

Node 24.18 changed Buffer.poolSize from 8 KiB to 64 KiB in https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/d3ef4122eefb6b293b72b348fc6ea4cb602622a5

Node uses the pool for Buffer allocations smaller than half the pool size. As a result, allocations below 32 KiB can now be views into a shared 64 KiB backing ArrayBuffer.

VS Code's VSBuffer preserves these pooled backing stores. Webview resource streaming then forwards Uint8Array views through transferable streams without copying just the visible byte range. Structured clone consequently serializes the full 64 KiB backing store.

Chromium's mojo_base::BigBuffer has a 64 KiB inline limit. The structured-clone envelope makes these payloads just above that limit, so each message switches from inline storage to writable shared memory.

On POSIX, each writable shared-memory region carries two file descriptors: its writable descriptor and a read-only descriptor used for conversion. Under a renderer RLIMIT_NOFILE of 1024, a burst of webview resource messages therefore consumes two descriptors per chunk.

Instrumentation of VS Code loading the Codex webview showed:

- 1,910 large CommonCloneableMessage serializations
- the dominant payload sizes were 65,556 and 65,557 bytes
- renderer descriptors increasing through 1021, 1022, and 1023..
- recvmsg() returning message bytes with MSG_CTRUNC once descriptors could no longer be installed
- subsequent resource failures and service-worker network errors.

Restoring the previous 8 KiB pool size prevents small VS Code buffers from retaining 64 KiB backing stores. Their structured-clone messages remain below BigBuffer's inline threshold and no longer require shared-memory descriptor pairs.

Instrumentation with this override removed the 65,556/65,557-byte message burst and avoided the clean renderer exit. Larger shared-memory messages can still exhaust descriptors under sufficiently heavy pressure, so this is a targeted mitigation rather than a replacement for the Mojo MSG_CTRUNC fix.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326092

title: Add voice mode started/stopped accessibility signals
body:
## Summary
Improves the accessibility signals for voice mode so screen reader users get correct, distinct feedback for entering/exiting voice mode versus starting/stopping dictation.

- Play the recording-started signal on every explicit or connect-initiated listen (keybinding or click), not only the first hands-free listen after connecting.
- Play the recording-stopped signal on explicit listening stops and when voice mode is explicitly exited (button/keybinding) while recording.
- Register dedicated `voiceModeStarted` / `voiceModeStopped` accessibility signals with their own announcements ("Voice Mode Started" / "Voice Mode Stopped"), separate from the generic dictation recording signals, so screen readers announce the right event.
- Add the corresponding `accessibility.signals.voiceModeStarted` / `accessibility.signals.voiceModeStopped` configuration entries.
- Thread an explicit vs internal `source` through `disconnect()` so only user-driven exits play the exit signal (internal teardown / error recovery stays silent).

title: fix: skip NES streamed edits for unknown target documents (fixes #326359)
body:
### Summary

The Next Edit Suggestion (NES) path throws `BugIndicatingError` ("An unexpected bug occurred.") with high frequency — **468 users / 3,245 hits** on `GitHub.copilot-chat` `0.57.0` (win32), plus ~920 more users across drifted sibling buckets (`d5ee2c95`, `a0c33451`, `0be6ac5b`, `f5de1e2e`).

The crash originates in `createDocStateLookupMap` (`extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts:148`): when a **streamed edit produced by the model** targets a document that is neither one of the request's projected documents nor an edit-history entry, the `CachedFunction` lookup falls through to `throw new BugIndicatingError()`. The streamed edit's `targetDocument` is model output — an untrusted boundary — so an unrecognised document id is a normal runtime possibility, not a programming invariant violation, and must not be reported as an unexpected bug.

The fix validates the model-produced `targetDocument` at the boundary (`_rebaseAndCacheStreamedEdit`) and skips unknown-document edits, returning `undefined` — a result both callers already handle gracefully as "edit could not be rebased".

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326359
Recommended reviewer: `@alexr00`

### Culprit Commit

The error is a genuinely **new** signature between `copilot-chat` `0.51.0` (baseline, absent) and `0.57.0` (VS Code 1.129.0), per the `errors-regression-scan` comment. The local checkout is a shallow (depth-1) clone, so per-line history before the checkout commit is not retrievable and an exact culprit SHA could not be confirmed offline. `git blame` attributes the current `createDocStateLookupMap` / `_rebaseAndCacheStreamedEdit` code (including the `throw new BugIndicatingError()` fall-through and the `xtabEditHistory` fallback loop) to recent work by **Alex Ross (`@alexr00`)**. The regression coincides with the cross-file / streamed-edit rebase refactor that introduced the `statePerDoc` lookup map keyed by model-supplied `targetDocument` ids.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["getNextEdit"] --> B["_getNextEditCanThrow"]
    B --> C["fetchNextEdit"]
    C --> D["_executeNewNextEditRequest"]
    D --> E["editStream: model streams StreamedEdit (targetDocument is model-produced)"]
    E --> F["processEdit(streamedEdit)"]
    F --> G["_rebaseAndCacheStreamedEdit"]
    G --> H["statePerDoc.get(streamedEdit.targetDocument) cache.ts:117"]
    H --> I{"doc in projectedDocuments or xtabEditHistory?"}
    I -->|yes| J["return DocState"]
    I -->|no| K["throw new BugIndicatingError() nextEditProvider.ts:148"]
    K --> L["unhandled: 'An unexpected bug occurred.' -> error telemetry"]
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts` | Producer boundary + crash site | Validate model-produced `targetDocument` before the `statePerDoc` lookup; skip unknown-document streamed edits instead of throwing. |

### Repro Steps

1. Trigger a Next Edit Suggestion in a file (inline edits / NES enabled).
2. Have the model stream a `StreamedEdit` whose `targetDocument` is not among the request's projected documents and not present as an `'edit'` entry in `xtabEditHistory` (e.g. a cross-file suggestion referencing a document that was not included in the request context).
3. `_rebaseAndCacheStreamedEdit` calls `statePerDoc.get(streamedEdit.targetDocument)`, the `CachedFunction` body falls through both lookups and throws `BugIndicatingError`, surfacing as the unhandled "An unexpected bug occurred." error.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts`):

- `createDocStateLookupMap` now returns `{ statePerDoc, isKnownDocument }`, where `isKnownDocument(id)` reports — without throwing — whether `statePerDoc.get(id)` can resolve a document (present in `projectedDocuments`, or an `'edit'` entry in `xtabEditHistory`). This reuses exactly the same membership logic the lookup body uses.
- `_rebaseAndCacheStreamedEdit` guards the model-produced `streamedEdit.targetDocument` with `isKnownDocument(...)` **before** calling `statePerDoc.get(...)`. When the target is unknown it logs a trace and returns `undefined`.
- Both call sites (`_executeNewNextEditRequest` and `_runSpeculativeProviderCall`) already treat an `undefined` result as "edit could not be rebased" and skip it, so the streamed edit is dropped cleanly rather than crashing the stream.

This is a guard clause placed at the **model-output boundary** — the point where untrusted data first enters the typed `DocumentId -> DocState` lookup — rather than at the crash site inside the cached function (fix at the data producer, not the crash site). The bypass site is `nextEditProvider.ts:148`, reached only via the model-supplied `targetDocument`; the guard sits at the sole producer path that can feed it an unvalidated id. The `throw new BugIndicatingError()` is deliberately left in place: it still correctly guards the internal invariant that `curDocId` (the active document, always a projected document) is resolvable, so a genuine internal misuse would still be reported. After this change, `nextEditProvider.ts:776` cannot forward an unknown model-produced `targetDocument` into `statePerDoc.get`, because the `isKnownDocument` guard returns early for exactly the ids that would otherwise reach the throw.

**Alternatives considered:**

- Wrapping the `statePerDoc.get(...)` call in `try/catch` — rejected because it hides the model-boundary condition behind exception handling and would also swallow genuine internal invariant violations, degrading telemetry instead of fixing the data path.
- Making the `CachedFunction` body return `undefined` for unknown ids — rejected because `DocState` is consumed as non-nullable at several sites (e.g. `statePerDoc.get(curDocId)`), so weakening the map's contract would ripple null-checks across unrelated, always-valid call sites.

### Recommended Owner

`@alexr00` — Alex Ross authored the current `createDocStateLookupMap` / `_rebaseAndCacheStreamedEdit` streamed-edit rebase code containing the crash site, and the regression tracks the cross-file streamed-edit refactor introduced between `0.51.0` and `0.57.0`.

title: fix: mark 'Language model unavailable' as expected chat error (fixes #326356)
body:
### Summary The `chatAgentError` telemetry bucket `chatagenterror-Language model unavailable` fires whenever `ExtHostChatAgents2.getModelForRequest` cannot resolve a language model for a chat request — thrown from `$invokeAgent` (and `$detectChatParticipant`). This is an **expected operational condition** (the user is not signed in, or no chat models have been contributed yet), not a code bug, but it was thrown as a generic `Error` and therefore published to error telemetry as noise. The fix marks it as a `ChatExpectedError` so the existing suppression path keeps it out of `chatAgentError` telemetry while still surfacing the user-facing message. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326356 Recommended reviewer: `@bryanchen-d` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing / re-bucketing | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | The `throw new Error('Language model unavailable')` in `getModelForRequest` is a long-standing pattern. The `isExpectedError` / `ChatExpectedError` suppression mechanism was added later ([`3727d0ce`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3727d0cef92f7788874bde4316754cfdc5d6a516), "add isExpectedError flag to suppress expected agent errors from telemetry", by `@bryanchen-d`, 2026-04-27). This throw was simply never opted into that mechanism, so it continued surfacing as a `chatAgentError` bucket. No single regression commit introduced the error path. | > No culprit commit — this is a pre-existing expected-error condition that was never registered with the `ChatExpectedError` telemetry-suppression channel. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Agent as Chat request participant Invoke as extHostChatAgents2.$invokeAgent participant Producer as getModelForRequest participant Main as mainThreadChatAgents2 Agent->>Invoke: invoke agent Invoke->>Producer: getModelForRequest(request, extension) Note over Producer: ⚠️ No user-selected model and
getDefaultLanguageModel() returns undefined
(user not signed in / no models) Producer-->>Invoke: throw new Error('Language model unavailable') Note over Invoke: 💥 Generic Error → errorCallstack packed,
isExpectedError NOT set Invoke->>Main: rpcResult { errorCallstack, errorName } Note over Main: publishes chatAgentError telemetry
(bucket: chatagenterror-Language model unavailable) ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostChatAgents2.ts` | root cause / producer | L948-L949 (pre-fix): `if (!model) { throw new Error('Language model unavailable'); }` — expected condition thrown as generic Error | | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostChatAgents2.ts` | crash site | L900/L950 (from shipped-commit stack): `getModelForRequest` / `$invokeAgent` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts` | telemetry emitter | L380-L397: `if (rpcResult?.errorCallstack && !rpcResult.errorDetails?.isExpectedError) { ... publicLogError2('chatAgentError', ...) }` — suppresses when `isExpectedError` is set | ### Repro Steps 1. Launch the Agents window / chat in a profile that is **not signed in** to Copilot (or that has no contributed chat models). 2. Send a chat request to an agent, or trigger participant detection. 3. `getModelForRequest` resolves no user-selected model and `getDefaultLanguageModel()` returns `undefined`, so `throw new Error('Language model unavailable')` fires. 4. Before this fix, the generic error is packed with a callstack and published as the `chatAgentError` telemetry event, producing the `chatagenterror-Language model unavailable` bucket. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostChatAgents2.ts`, `getModelForRequest`: the fix is applied at the **data producer** (where the invalid/expected state is first detected), not at the crash site or in a downstream `try/catch`. Instead of throwing a generic `Error`, the "no model available" case now throws an error whose `name` is set to `ChatExpectedError`. `$invokeAgent` already maps `e.name === 'ChatExpectedError'` to `errorDetails.isExpectedError = true`, and `mainThreadChatAgents2` already skips publishing the `chatAgentError` event when that flag is set (the existing suppression channel added for rate-limit / quota / connectivity / "cloud agent not enabled" conditions). This removes the bucket from error telemetry while preserving the user-facing message and the `logService.error` log entry — no logging is removed and no error is swallowed in a `try/catch`. This is the intended use of the `ChatExpectedError` mechanism: a genuinely expected, user-actionable operational condition opts out of bug telemetry rather than being silenced. **Alternatives considered**: - Gating the `logService.error(e, ...)` call or the `chatAgentError` emission on the message string `'Language model unavailable'` — rejected because string-matching in the consumer is brittle and puts the decision in the wrong place; the producer already knows the condition is expected. - Wrapping the `getModelForRequest` call in a `try/catch` that returns a benign result — rejected because it hides the condition from the user-facing error surface and masks the state instead of classifying it. ### Recommended Owner `@bryanchen-d` — owner of the `chatAgentError` telemetry event (`owner: 'bryanchen-d'` in `mainThreadChatAgents2.ts`) and author of the `isExpectedError` / `ChatExpectedError` suppression mechanism this fix uses. Active VS Code team member; already assigned to the issue. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29589655953) · 2K AIC · ⌖ 34.2 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: Exit Voice Mode Listening When Session Focus Changes
body:
## Summary
Voice Mode no longer "follows" focus into a newly selected session. When the active session changes while Voice Mode is listening, we stop following it — and, crucially, we handle any speech the user already spoke so it is neither lost nor misrouted.

## Behavior on a session focus change while listening
- **User has already spoken** (a non-empty user partial transcript exists) → the turn is **finalized and submitted to the original session** the user was dictating into, via `finishListeningAndSubmitTo(session)`. Routing is pinned to that session, taking priority over the user-picked target and the currently focused session, so words can never leak into the newly focused session.
- **Nothing dictated yet** → `discardListening()`: the in-flight press is aborted **without** sending `ptt_end`, so the backend never finalizes buffered audio into a `send_to_chat`. A stray `send_to_chat` (e.g. the backend VAD-auto-ended the turn) is dropped for a short window.
- **Standard chat view only:** an idle hands-free listen may still follow a fresh untitled **"New Chat"** session before any dictation starts (the common "start listening, then click New Chat" flow).
- An explicit **target session** still wins — focus changes don't disturb it. The WebSocket stays connected, so the user can resume without a new handshake. The explicit **Stop Listening** button still finalizes normally.

## Why submit-instead-of-discard
A pure discard threw away words the user had already spoken when focus changed out from under them (e.g. a background agent session steals focus). Submitting to the original session honors the user's words while still preventing the misroute. The pin is one-shot (consumed by the next `send_to_chat`) and cleared on the next `pttDown` or after a 15s expiry.

## Applies to
- Standard chat view (`ChatViewPane`)
- Agents window (`voiceBridge.contribution.ts`)
- New controller ops in `voiceSessionController.ts`: `discardListening()` and `finishListeningAndSubmitTo()`

## Validation
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck --pretty false`
- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/voiceBridge.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widgetHosts/viewPane/chatViewPane.ts`
- `npm run precommit`

title: Further Unify Model Picker Architecture
body:
## Summary This further unifies model selection and restoration across the editor/workbench and Agents window. - Adds one shared pure model-selection policy in `vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/modelSelection.ts`. - Shares catalog resolution, configured-model matching, initial precedence, pending state, and fallback semantics across `ChatInputPart` and `SessionModelSelectionModel`. - Uses the shared lifecycle transition in the Sessions adapter for existing-session repair, new-chat repush, and late catalog changes. - Replaces the ambiguous provider `isResolved` signal with `desiredModelResolution`: `notRequested`, `pending`, `available`, or `unavailable`. - Adds provider-owned `modelTarget` metadata so provider-scoped model pools use the same remembered-selection key as their Workbench counterpart. - Unifies remembered-model persistence through `chatSelectedModel.ts`, using profile-scoped user storage keyed by chat location and optional model target, with lazy migration from legacy Workbench and Sessions keys. - Keeps a remembered Copilot model pending while model discovery is still loading instead of committing an early BYOK fallback. - Treats automatic first-model fallback as provisional so a later provider default or Auto model can replace it. - In Sessions, persists only provider-accepted explicit user choices; automatic restore, repair, and fallback effects update the provider without overwriting the remembered preference. - Cancels pending restoration when the user explicitly selects another model. - Routes phone model actions through the owning Workbench or Sessions selection adapter instead of maintaining a separate persistence path. - Removes the duplicate Agents-window selection policy and separates shared policy, shared storage, surface adapters, input utilities, and picker presentation by ownership. Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326260 ## Previous Architecture The workbench and Agents window used independent restoration policies. They shared picker presentation, but each surface separately interpreted model readiness, precedence, fallback, and persistence. ```mermaid flowchart LR Registry[Language model registry and cache] Providers[ISessionsProvider snapshots] Workbench[Editor and Workbench
ChatInputPart] WorkbenchPolicy[chatModelSelectionLogic
workbench restore and fallback policy] Agents[Agents window
ModelPickerModel] AgentsPolicy[modelPickerSelection
Agents restore and fallback policy] Registry --> WorkbenchPolicy --> Workbench Providers --> AgentsPolicy --> Agents WorkbenchPolicy -. duplicated semantics .- AgentsPolicy ``` This allowed the two surfaces to diverge. In particular, the Agents window could treat a partial model list as complete, select the first BYOK model, and persist it before Copilot models arrived. ## New Architecture Both surfaces now use the same pure catalog-resolution, matching, initial-selection, and fallback building blocks. The Sessions adapter also delegates catalog-driven lifecycle transitions to that shared policy. Both adapters use one canonical remembered-selection storage contract while retaining the application and lifecycle concerns that genuinely differ. ```mermaid flowchart TD SharedPolicy[common/modelSelection.ts
resolution, matching, precedence, transition effects] SharedStorage[common/chatSelectedModel.ts
canonical remembered-selection storage] Registry[Language model registry and cache] Providers[ISessionsProvider.getModelsSnapshot
desiredModelResolution and modelTarget] WorkbenchAdapter[ChatInputPart
workbench lifecycle adapter] AgentsAdapter[SessionModelSelectionModel
Sessions provider adapter] PickerUI[modelPicker folder
widget, items, hover, presentation] Registry --> WorkbenchAdapter Providers --> AgentsAdapter WorkbenchAdapter --> SharedPolicy AgentsAdapter --> SharedPolicy WorkbenchAdapter --> SharedStorage AgentsAdapter --> SharedStorage WorkbenchAdapter --> PickerUI AgentsAdapter --> PickerUI ``` The shared policy owns: 1. Catalog readiness and identifier resolution. 2. Configured model matching, including model families and Auto. 3. Initial configured, restored, pending, unavailable, and fallback precedence. 4. Automatic selection provenance, including provisional first-available fallback. 5. Sessions lifecycle transitions for stale-model repair, existing-session restoration, and new-chat repush. 6. Selection reasons and provider effects. The shared storage helper owns canonical `(location, modelTarget)` keys, profile-scoped user storage, and migration from the previous application-scoped Workbench keys. The Sessions adapter additionally migrates its previous provider/session-type key into that canonical store. `ChatInputPart` and `SessionModelSelectionModel` remain separate adapters because their model inputs, application paths, and session lifecycles differ. Workbench controls its wait-listener lifecycle and input-model synchronization. Sessions controls provider snapshots and writes, and remembers only provider-accepted explicit choices. Providers expose the concrete `modelTarget` for their model pool so both surfaces address the same remembered selection. ## Behavior When BYOK models arrive before a remembered Copilot model: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Catalog as Model catalog participant Policy as Shared selection policy participant Picker as Model picker participant Storage as Remembered selection Catalog->>Policy: BYOK available, Copilot still pending Policy->>Picker: Keep remembered selection pending Policy->>Storage: Do not overwrite preference Catalog->>Policy: Copilot model becomes available Policy->>Picker: Apply remembered Copilot model Policy->>Storage: Preserve remembered preference ``` When there is no remembered choice, an early BYOK model may be applied provisionally so the session remains usable. A later provider default or Auto model replaces that provisional fallback. In the Sessions adapter, neither automatic choice is written as a user preference. If the user explicitly chooses a model while discovery is pending, that explicit choice wins and cancels pending restoration. In Sessions, the provider is updated first and the canonical remembered preference is written only after the provider accepts the change. ## Validation - `npm run typecheck-client` - `npm run transpile-client` - `npm run valid-layers-check` - VS Code hygiene checks for all changed TypeScript files - Affected unit tests covering shared selection policy and storage, Agents selection coordination, provider snapshots, quota notifications, and Sessions management

title: Git - show staged type changes in the Source Control view
body:
Staging a type change — for example replacing a symlink with a regular file and then `git add`-ing it — left the file invisible in the Source Control view. `git status` reports a staged type change as `T ` (T in the index column), but the index-side parser in `updateModelState` only handled `M`/`A`/`D`/`R`/`C`, so the resource was silently dropped. The unstaged case has shown correctly since #187714 (2023), which added `Status.TYPE_CHANGED` for the working-tree side only.

This adds a matching `Status.INDEX_TYPE_CHANGED` and routes a staged `T` into the index group, mirroring how `INDEX_MODIFIED` relates to `MODIFIED`: staged color (`gitDecoration.stageModifiedResourceForeground`), the `(Index)` diff title, HEAD↔index diff, and the existing type-changed glyph. The new value is appended to the end of the `Status` enum so no existing ordinal shifts.

Fixes #91100

### How I verified

Added a smoke test covering the issue body's exact steps (symlink → commit → replace with a regular file → stage), asserting the unstaged change surfaces as `TYPE_CHANGED` and the staged one as `INDEX_TYPE_CHANGED`. The full git integration suite passes locally (58 passing, including the new test). Skipped on Windows, where creating a symlink needs elevation.

title: Mermaid code blocks are not rendered by the extension, while VS Code's native Markdown preview renders them correctly
body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

The extension does not render Mermaid code blocks in Markdown, even though the exact same Markdown is rendered correctly by VS Code's native Markdown preview.

This creates inconsistent behavior between the built-in renderer and the extension. Since Mermaid support is already available natively in VS Code, I expected the extension to render the diagrams as well.

### Expected Behavior

Mermaid code blocks should be rendered as diagrams, matching the behavior of VS Code's native Markdown preview.

### Actual Behavior

The extension displays the Mermaid code block as plain text (or does not render it at all), while the native VS Code Markdown preview renders the diagram correctly.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Markdown file.
2. Add a Mermaid code block, for example:

````markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Start] --> B[Process]
    B --> C[End]
```
````

3. Open the Markdown using the extension's preview/rendering feature.
4. Observe that the Mermaid diagram is not rendered.
5. Open the same file using VS Code's native Markdown Preview.
6. Observe that the Mermaid diagram renders correctly.

### Expected Result

Both the extension and VS Code's native Markdown preview should render the Mermaid diagram identically.

### Actual Result

Only the native Markdown preview renders the diagram. The extension fails to render it.

### Additional Information

This appears to be a missing or incomplete Mermaid rendering implementation in the extension. Since VS Code already supports Mermaid diagrams natively, it would be great if the extension could provide equivalent rendering behavior for compatibility and consistency.

Thank you for looking into this issue.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->

<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

* VS Code Version: VSCode-win32-x64-1.129.0
* OS Version: Windows 11
* Installation type: Windows ZIP
* Regular installed VS Code also present: Yes

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the regular Windows version of VS Code.
2. Download and extract the Windows ZIP version of VS Code to another folder.
3. Create a `data` folder next to `Code.exe` to enable portable mode.
4. Start the portable version by running its `Code.exe`.
5. Open the Windows Start menu and launch VS Code from the existing VS Code entry.

Expected behavior:

Starting the portable version should not modify the Start menu entry belonging to the normally installed version.

The existing Start menu shortcut should continue to point to the regular installed copy of VS Code. The portable copy should remain self-contained inside its extracted folder and should not modify the host system configuration.

Actual behavior:

After starting the portable `Code.exe`, the existing VS Code entry in the Windows Start menu is overwritten or changed so that it opens the portable copy instead of the normally installed version.

This behavior defeats the purpose of portable mode. A portable application should remain self-contained and non-invasive. It should not overwrite Start menu shortcuts, replace the default installed application, or modify the system setup without explicit user permission.

Portable mode is enabled simply by extracting the ZIP archive and adding a `data` folder next to `Code.exe`. Running that portable executable should not interfere with a separate installed copy of VS Code.

title: SCM Changes view does not restore repository/group collapsed state after reload

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes — reproduced in an isolated profile with no third-party SCM automation. Better Git's automatic SCM tree management was disabled, and its command trace remained empty during startup and restart.

- VS Code Version: 1.129.0 (commit `125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7`, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a workspace where the main **Source Control: Changes** view contains at least two Git repositories or worktrees.
2. Wait for all repositories and their resource groups to finish loading.
3. Leave one repository expanded and manually collapse another repository header. A mixed resource-group state can also be used, for example leaving **Changes** expanded in one repository and collapsed in another.
4. Run **Developer: Reload Window**, or fully quit and reopen the same workspace.
5. Wait for Git repository discovery to settle.

## Expected

The main Changes tree restores the previous mixed expanded/collapsed state for repository headers and resource groups.

## Actual

Previously collapsed repositories and groups reopen. After the asynchronous SCM reconstruction settles, `scm.viewState2` is overwritten with the now-expanded tree state, so the user's collapsed choices are lost.

I reproduced this with eight repositories in an isolated profile. The pre-restart mixed state was present in `scm.viewState2`; after a full process restart every discovered repository/group started expanded.

## Regression history and likely mechanism

This exact behavior was previously reported in:

- #102831 — collapse a Git repository, reload, and it is expanded again
- #106196 — retain collapsed state of SCM providers across reloads

Those issues were closed as fixed after #89145 / #89313 implemented persisted tree collapse state.

The main Changes view was later migrated to `AsyncDataTree` in #197349. Current code:

- stores `this.tree.getViewState()` in `scm.viewState2`;
- persists only an `expanded` ID list for expansion state;
- configures repositories, resource groups, and resource folders as expanded by default.

Relevant code:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmViewPane.ts#L1640-L1643
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmViewPane.ts#L1960-L1977
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts#L1287-L1290
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts#L1349-L1355

An ID omitted from `expanded` because the user collapsed it therefore falls through to the expanded default, just like a genuinely new node. This appears to regress the view-state-aware collapse behavior added by #89313.

## Related but distinct issues

- #270454 / #305267 concerns auto-reveal reopening **Staged Changes** when an active staged file is open; it does not cover cold-start restoration.
- #322318 / #322319 concerns the separate **Source Control Repositories** view, not the main Changes tree.
- #271554 / #307887 / #320526 concerns repository visibility selection and late-discovered worktrees. Hiding repositories can persist in the fast path, but hidden headers disappear entirely and it is not mixed expansion-state restoration.

## Workaround

**Source Control → View & Sort → Repositories** can hide unwanted repositories and persisted a two-of-eight selection in isolated restart tests. It is only a partial workaround: the headers are removed instead of remaining visible-but-collapsed, and late worktree discovery is separately tracked by #271554.

`scm.autoReveal: false` does not restore the cold-start collapse state. Extensions also have no public per-repository or per-group collapse API; only global collapse-all/expand-all behavior is safely available.

I do not currently have VS Code Insiders installed on this Mac, so the direct runtime reproduction above is from current Stable 1.129.0. The linked current-main code still contains the state/default interaction described above.

Open the normal VS Code Chat view and confirm the custom models appear in the model picker and can be selected and used. 3. Fully quit VS Code (⌘Q) and all Agents windows, then reopen (a plain `Reload Window` is not enough, per the setting docs). 4. Open the **Agents** window (`Chat: Open Agents Window` / "Open in Agents"). 5. Start a new session and select the **Copilot** agent. 6. title: VS IDE crashes after update 1.129.0
body:
**Description**

After updating VS Code on Linux Mint, the IDE crashes repeatedly. Crash logs show application hangs before a forced restart.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Install the latest VS Code on Linux Mint (e.g., 21.2).
2. Open any project or create a new file.
3. Observe the editor functioning normally until it crashes.

**Expected Behavior**
VS Code should remain stable without causing OS-level crashes.

**Actual Behavior**
VS Code crashes multiple times after the update, requiring manual restart of the IDE.

**Environment**
- Linux Mint 21.2 (based on Ubuntu 22.04)
- VS Code version: latest (e.g., 1.94.0)
- Extensions: none installed}

title: fix: restore 8 KiB Node buffer pool on linux

labels.name: candidate
labels.description: Issue identified as probable candidate for fixing in the next release

body:
Node 24.18 changed Buffer.poolSize from 8 KiB to 64 KiB in https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/d3ef4122eefb6b293b72b348fc6ea4cb602622a5

Node uses the pool for Buffer allocations smaller than half the pool size. As a result, allocations below 32 KiB can now be views into a shared 64 KiB backing ArrayBuffer.

VS Code's VSBuffer preserves these pooled backing stores. Webview resource streaming then forwards Uint8Array views through transferable streams without copying just the visible byte range. Structured clone consequently serializes the full 64 KiB backing store.

Chromium's mojo_base::BigBuffer has a 64 KiB inline limit. The structured-clone envelope makes these payloads just above that limit, so each message switches from inline storage to writable shared memory.

On POSIX, each writable shared-memory region carries two file descriptors: its writable descriptor and a read-only descriptor used for conversion. Under a renderer RLIMIT_NOFILE of 1024, a burst of webview resource messages therefore consumes two descriptors per chunk.

Instrumentation of VS Code loading the Codex webview showed:

- 1,910 large CommonCloneableMessage serializations
- the dominant payload sizes were 65,556 and 65,557 bytes
- renderer descriptors increasing through 1021, 1022, and 1023..
- recvmsg() returning message bytes with MSG_CTRUNC once descriptors could no longer be installed
- subsequent resource failures and service-worker network errors.

Restoring the previous 8 KiB pool size prevents small VS Code buffers from retaining 64 KiB backing stores. Their structured-clone messages remain below BigBuffer's inline threshold and no longer require shared-memory descriptor pairs.

Instrumentation with this override removed the 65,556/65,557-byte message burst and avoided the clean renderer exit. Larger shared-memory messages can still exhaust descriptors under sufficiently heavy pressure, so this is a targeted mitigation rather than a replacement for the Mojo MSG_CTRUNC fix.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326092

title: feature: webview without service worker

feature: webview without service workers
body: Currently, in VSCode, webviews are implemented via two iframes and a service worker. It seems it could be possible to improve webview loading performance and fix errors by using a single iframe, instead a service workers and two iframes. Note: The change would only affect VS Code electron, not VS Code in the browser. ### Benchmarks Benchmarks from a prototype PR using a single iframe indicate ~25% percent load time improvement for webviews. For example for the Codex webview: ### Other Benefits Another benefit would be that it avoids a lot of weird webview service workers errors like: - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326092 - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/125993 ### Breaking changes It seems there shouldn't be any breaking changes. The feature would be opt in for extensions.

title: Fix macOS test flake
SSH askpass shows yes/no host-fingerprint prompt instead of PIN input for FIDO2/security-key authentication

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (this is a bug in the built-in `git` extension itself, which `--disable-extensions` does not disable)

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.129.0 (commit 125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7, x64), built-in Git extension v10.0.0
- OS Version: Linux (CachyOS, kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure an SSH remote authenticated with an `ed25519-sk`/`ecdsa-sk` (FIDO2 security key) registered with `verify-required` (PIN + touch), with `git.useIntegratedAskPass` left at its default (`true`).
2. Trigger a `git fetch`/`git push` in the Source Control panel that requires signing with that key.
3. OpenSSH's `ssh-sk-helper` prompts for the key's PIN with the text `Enter PIN for authenticator:`.
4. VS Code shows a yes/no "Are you sure you want to continue connecting?" quick pick instead of a PIN input box (there is no way to enter a PIN), and authentication fails.

Root cause: in `extensions/git/dist/main.js`, `handleSSHAskpass()` only renders a text input box when the prompt matches `/passphrase/i`; every other prompt falls through to the yes/no "continue connecting" quick pick meant for host-key confirmation. OpenSSH's FIDO2 PIN prompt text ("Enter PIN for authenticator:") does not contain "passphrase", so it is misclassified.

Expected: a password-style input box should be shown for the PIN prompt, the same way it already works for `Enter passphrase for key ...` prompts.

Workaround: set `"git.useIntegratedAskPass": false` so the OS-level `SSH_ASKPASS` helper (e.g. `x11-ssh-askpass`) handles the prompt instead of VS Code's own UI.

title: Return MethodNotFound for unsupported Agent Host requests
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Unsupported JSON-RPC requests sent before the Agent Host handshake currently receive no response, causing clients to wait until timeout. Unknown requests after initialization also use the incorrect `InternalError` code.

- **Request dispatch**
  - Return `MethodNotFound` (`-32601`) for unsupported pre-initialize requests.
  - Use the same error code and message after initialization.

- **Coverage**
  - Verify consistent unknown-method responses across the initialization boundary.

title: Agent Host: Return an error for unsupported requests before initialize

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

When a client sends a JSON-RPC request other than `initialize`, `reconnect`, `ping`, or `_vscodeUpgrade` before completing the Agent Host Protocol handshake, the agent host currently stays silent. Please return a JSON-RPC error instead, preferably `MethodNotFound` (`-32601`) for an unknown method (or an explicit not-initialized error if that is a better protocol contract).

A silent response leaves generic JSON-RPC clients waiting until their own timeout and makes an incompatible protocol/handshake look like a transport failure.

### Standalone Node.js reproduction

```js
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:4123?tkn=<connection-token>');

ws.addEventListener('open', () => {
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({
    jsonrpc: '2.0',
    id: 1,
    method: 'notARealMethod',
    params: { channel: 'ahp-root://' },
  }));
});

ws.addEventListener('message', event => {
  console.log(String(event.data));
});
```

Observed against the local VS Code agent host: the WebSocket opens, but no response arrives within 3 seconds.

This was also verified after a valid AHP `initialize`: the same unknown request then receives an immediate error. The current post-initialize response uses `-32603` (JSON-RPC Internal error):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "error": {
    "code": -32603,
    "message": "Unknown method: notARealMethod"
  }
}
```

The silent behavior is therefore specific to pre-initialize dispatch. Ideally, unknown methods should consistently return JSON-RPC `MethodNotFound` (`-32601`) rather than `InternalError` (`-32603`).

### Expected

The server responds to every JSON-RPC request with either a result or an error, including before initialization. For the request above, for example:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": -32601,
    "message": "Method not found"
  }
}
```

title: Renderer crashes with SIGBUS (code 135) shortly after workspace startup — memcpy reads past EOF of a /dev/shm shared-memory region (regression in 1.129.0)
body:
- **Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?**: Not verified — the crash is intermittent (minutes to hours between occurrences), so a clean negative with `--disable-extensions` was not obtainable.
- **VS Code Version**: 1.129.0 (commit `125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7`), RPM `code-1.129.0-1784075033.el8.x86_64` from packages.microsoft.com
- **OS Version**: Fedora Linux 44, kernel 7.1.3-201.fc44.x86_64
- **Session**: KDE Plasma on Wayland (`--ozone-platform=wayland`), dual GPU, 61 GB RAM

## Summary

Since updating to 1.129.0, the workbench renderer process intermittently crashes with **SIGBUS** (exit code 135) within ~35–75 seconds of opening a workspace. The window first goes unresponsive, sometimes recovers, then the renderer dies. The subsequent extension-host restart loop makes it look like an extension problem, but core-dump analysis shows the renderer is killed while copying data out of a Chromium shared-memory segment whose backing `/dev/shm` file is smaller than the declared region size.

Downgrading to 1.128.1 on the same machine/OS/kernel makes the problem disappear (regression). No other Chromium-based browser on this machine (same kernel, same /dev/shm) has ever produced a SIGBUS core dump.

## main.log at crash time

```
2026-07-17 10:11:37.596 [info] StorageMainService: creating application shared storage
...
2026-07-17 10:12:12.019 [error] CodeWindow: detected unresponsive
2026-07-17 10:12:17.683 [error] CodeWindow: recovered from unresponsive
2026-07-17 10:12:48.493 [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 135)
```

## Core-dump forensics (two independent crashes)

Both cores show the renderer's main thread inside glibc's AVX-512 `memcpy`/`memmove`, faulting on the **first (tail-first) access** of a copy whose *source* is a Chromium shared-memory mapping and whose *destination* is inside the V8 heap cage:

```
Program terminated with signal SIGBUS, Bus error.
=> 0x7fee1619f512:  vmovdqu64 -0x40(%rsi,%rdx,1),%zmm24     # rip inside /usr/lib64/libc.so.6
```

**Crash A — 2026-07-16 18:06 (PID 26243, GPU compositing enabled):**

| item | value |
|---|---|
| source `rsi` | `0x7fecfa50d000` = base of mapping `/dev/shm/.org.chromium.Chromium.cdf0B0 (deleted)` (`0x7fecfa50d000`–`0x7fecfa7f8000`, len `0x2eb000`) |
| copy length `rdx` | `0x2ea68c` (3,057,292 bytes) |
| destination `rdi` | `0x288404a04000` (V8 heap) |
| `si_code` | **2 = `BUS_ADRERR`** |
| `si_addr` | `0x7fecfa7f764c` = exactly `rsi + rdx - 0x40` |

**Crash B — 2026-07-17 10:12 (PID 190556, `disable-hardware-acceleration: true` active, renderer cmdline contains `--disable-gpu-compositing`):**

| item | value |
|---|---|
| source `rsi` | `0x7f0418cda000` (Chromium shm mapping) |
| copy length `rdx` | `0x19a8a` (105,098 bytes) |
| destination `rdi` | `0x131c099a0000` (V8 heap) |
| `si_code` | **2 = `BUS_ADRERR`** |
| `si_addr` | `0x7f0418cf3a4a` = exactly `rsi + rdx - 0x40` |

My interpretation: `BUS_ADRERR` on a tmpfs-backed read means the touched page lies beyond the backing file's end. In both crashes the fault hits the page containing the claimed end of the payload, i.e. the `/dev/shm` segment's actual file size is at least one page shorter than the size the renderer-side consumer was told (backward copy touches the highest page first, so the actual file may be shorter still). This looks like a size mismatch between producer and consumer of a shared-memory region (mojo BigBuffer / large IPC transfer path), not memory corruption.

I tried it with GPU compositing enabled and disabled and got the same issues. It's not a hardware issue.

## System-level causes ruled out (verified on the affected machine)

- **Hardware memory error**: `si_code` is `BUS_ADRERR` (2), not `BUS_MCEERR_AR` (4); no kernel `Memory failure`/MCE/EDAC events logged.
- **/dev/shm exhaustion**: 31 GB tmpfs, <100 MB used; per-user tmpfs quota (24.6 GB) far from exhausted.
- **Swap/zram failure**: swap 0 B used (61 GB RAM), no I/O errors.
- **shmem THP bugs**: `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/shmem_enabled` = `never`.
- **Generic tmpfs breakage**: a minimal reproducer (create file in /dev/shm, `ftruncate` to `0x19a8a`, `mmap`, read at offset `0x19a4a` in the EOF page, plus full write/read-back) passes cleanly.
- **Kernel regression**: crash-free VS Code sessions occurred on the same kernel build; the kernel update in that window contains only unrelated (xfs/media) changes.
- **Machine-wide Chromium issue**: full `coredumpctl` history shows SIGBUS only for `/usr/share/code/code` (3×, all after 1.129.0 first ran); never for actual browsers.

## Timeline / regression evidence

- 1.129.0 first launched 2026-07-16 17:03 (local); first SIGBUS 18:01 the same day, two more within 24 h.
- Crashes occur during workspace startup/restore. The affected workspace had unusually large state (22 MB `state.vscdb`, 1.8 GB  `workspaceStorage`), i.e. large IPC payloads into the renderer at startup; this may only affect trigger probability.
- After downgrading to `code-1.128.1-1784039574.el8`: no further crashes (same OS, kernel, extensions, workspace).

## Possibly related issues (all opened against 1.129.0 in the last two days)

- #326241
- #326309
- #326174
- #326113

body: ## Environment Information **Visual Studio Code** Version: 1.129.0 Commit: 125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7 Date: 2026-07-15T00:08:44Z (2 days ago) Electron: 42.6.0 ElectronBuildId: 14623276 Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.0 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 OS: Linux x64 7.0.0-28-generic --- # Bug Report ## Title **VS Code enters an infinite crash/relaunch loop when opening a second window on Linux Mint Cinnamon with an NVIDIA GPU** ## Environment - VS Code Version: 1.129.0 - Commit: `125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7` - Electron: 42.6.0 - Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 - Node.js: 24.18.0 - OS: Linux Mint (Cinnamon) - Kernel: Linux x64 7.0.0-28-generic - GPU: NVIDIA (proprietary driver) ## Description Whenever I open a second VS Code window, the application enters an infinite crash/relaunch loop. The newly opened window alternates between the following two dialogs: ``` The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'clean-exit', code: '0') We are sorry for the inconvenience. You can open a new empty window to start again. ``` followed by: ``` The window is not responding You can reopen or close the window or keep waiting. ``` Clicking **Reopen** causes the same sequence to repeat indefinitely. The second window never becomes usable. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Launch Visual Studio Code. 2. Open any folder or workspace. 3. Open a second VS Code window (File → New Window). 4. Observe the behavior. ## Expected Behavior The second window should open normally and become fully responsive. ## Actual Behavior The second window immediately exits with: ``` reason: 'clean-exit', code: '0' ``` It then becomes unresponsive, displaying the "The window is not responding" dialog. Choosing **Reopen** restarts the same cycle indefinitely. ## Frequency - Reproduces every time. - 100% reproducible. ## Additional Information - The issue only affects the newly opened window. - The original VS Code window remains functional. - The behavior started after updating to VS Code 1.129.0. - The system is running Linux Mint Cinnamon with the proprietary NVIDIA driver. ## Version Information ``` Version: 1.129.0 Commit: 125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7 Date: 2026-07-15T00:08:44Z Electron: 42.6.0 ElectronBuildId: 14623276 Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.0 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 OS: Linux x64 7.0.0-28-generic ``` ## Error Messages ``` The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'clean-exit', code: '0') We are sorry for the inconvenience. You can open a new empty window to start again. ``` ``` The window is not responding You can reopen or close the window or keep waiting. ``` ## Additional Testing I performed a few additional tests to isolate the issue: | Launch option | Result | |---------------|--------| | Default | `reason: 'clean-exit', code: '0'` | | `--disable-gpu` | `reason: 'crashed', code: '7'` | | `--disable-gpu-compositing` | `reason: 'clean-exit', code: '0'` | Disabling GPU compositing does not change the behavior. Disabling GPU changes the failure mode from a clean renderer exit (`clean-exit`, code `0`) to an actual renderer crash (`crashed`, code `7`), but the second window still cannot be opened. The issue remains 100% reproducible regardless of these launch options.

title: Ctrl+C/V/X don't work in integrated browser panel (browserView) under non-Latin keyboard layouts (e.g. Cyrillic)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: browser-integration
labels.description: Web browsing features integrated into VS Code (e.g. integrated browser)

body:
<!-- Generated with repro details verified locally against v1.129.0 -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.129.0 (commit 125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations 10.0.26200

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set the active Windows input language to a Cyrillic-script layout — or any layout where `Ctrl+C` produces `event.key !== "c"`, e.g. `event.key === "с"` on a Cyrillic layout.
2. Open the integrated browser panel (`browserView`, e.g. via "Simple Browser: Show" or any built-in preview that uses the browser panel) and navigate to any page with selectable text.
3. Select some text.
4. Press `Ctrl+C`.

**Expected:** Selected text is copied to the clipboard, same as when the English layout is active.

**Actual:** Nothing is copied. Right-click → Copy from the context menu works fine regardless of layout, and `Ctrl+C` works fine once the input language is switched to English — so this is specific to non-Latin keyboard layouts.

This also confirms it's not an OS/Chromium-level issue: copying with `Ctrl+C` under the same Cyrillic layout works normally in Edge/Chrome outside of VS Code.

## Root Cause

`src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-browser/preload-browserView.ts` decides whether to let `Ctrl+C/V/X/A/Z/Y` be handled natively by the page, or to `preventDefault()` and forward the key event to the workbench instead, by checking the **produced character**:

```ts
const key = event.key.toLowerCase();
const keySetsToCheck = [
	nativeCtrlCmdKeybindings[isMac ? 'mac' : 'nonMac'].always,
	nativeCtrlCmdKeybindings[isMac ? 'mac' : 'nonMac'][event.shiftKey ? 'withShift' : 'noShift'],
];
if (keySetsToCheck.some(set => set.has(key))) {
	return; // let the browser handle it natively
}
```

`nativeCtrlCmdKeybindings` only contains Latin characters (`'a', 'c', 'v', 'x', 'z', 'y'`). Under a Cyrillic keyboard layout, `Ctrl+C` produces `event.key === "с"` (Cyrillic), which never matches `'c'`. As a result the event falls through to `event.preventDefault()` + forwarding to the workbench, where there is no command that performs copy for the browser panel's page content — so the keystroke is silently swallowed.

This is the same class of layout-dependent bug the `keyboard.dispatch: "keyCode"` setting exists to work around for the main editor/workbench keybinding resolution — but that setting has no effect here, since this check is a separate, hardcoded character comparison in the preload script, not routed through the keybinding service.

## Suggested Fix

Use the physical key (`event.code`) instead of the produced character (`event.key`) when checking against the Latin letter sets, since `event.code` is layout-independent:

```ts
const key = /^Key[A-Z]$/.test(event.code)
	? event.code.slice(3).toLowerCase()
	: event.key.toLowerCase();
```

This only changes behavior for the lettered shortcuts (`a/c/v/x/z/y`); the `always` set (arrows, backspace, delete, home/end) is unaffected since those are already layout-independent via `event.key`.

I verified this fix locally by patching the compiled `preload-browserView.js` in an installed copy of VS Code 1.129.0 (replacing `t.key.toLowerCase()` with the `t.code`-based check above) — `Ctrl+C/V/X` in the browser panel then worked correctly under the Cyrillic layout, with no regression observed on the English layout.

title: Fix dependencies on Linux
Make command risk assessment explanations respect `github.copilot.chat.localeOverride`
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

The command risk assessment explanation shown in the terminal tool confirmation dialog should respect the `github.copilot.chat.localeOverride` setting.

For example, when the following setting is configured:

```json
{
  "github.copilot.chat.localeOverride": "ja"
}
```

regular Copilot Chat responses are displayed in Japanese, but the AI-generated command risk assessment explanation is still displayed in English.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `github.copilot.chat.localeOverride` to `ja`.
2. Enable command risk assessment with `chat.tools.riskAssessment.enabled`.
3. Ask the agent to run a command that requires confirmation.
4. Open the terminal tool confirmation dialog.
5. Observe that the risk assessment explanation is displayed in English.

### Expected behavior

The risk assessment explanation should be generated in the language specified by `github.copilot.chat.localeOverride`.

Alternatively, a separate setting could be provided for selecting the language used by risk assessment explanations.

### Why this is important

Risk assessment explanations are safety-critical information intended to help users decide whether a command should be allowed.

Users who configure Copilot Chat to use their preferred language may not fully understand an English-only risk explanation, particularly when it describes destructive operations, remote state changes, package installation, or other security risks.

The risk level color and icon are useful, but users also need to understand the explanation describing what the command will actually do.

### Related issues

* #280512 — Slash commands do not respect `github.copilot.chat.localeOverride`
* #313991 — Terminal command risk assessment

title: 1.129.0 renderer crashes repeatedly (SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGTRAP) when attaching to a Dev Container; downgrade to 1.128.1 fixes it

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: 
Not tested — the crash occurs during the Dev Containers attach handshake itself, before the workspace/extensions of the target folder are relevant. Bundled `ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers` (0.466.0) is required to reproduce at all.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.129.0 (commit unknown — installed via apt, `code:amd64 1.129.0-1784074987`), crash does not reproduce on 1.128.1
- OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-40-generic
- Dev Containers extension: 0.466.0
- Remote Docker context (SSH tunnel to a remote Docker daemon), attaching to an already-running container

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.17, Wayland), attach VS Code Desktop to an already-running Dev Container (`ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers`, "Attach to Running Container", authority `attached-container`) over a container whose Docker daemon is reached via an SSH-tunneled `docker context` (not local Docker).
2. Repeat attach attempts (reload window / reopen).
3. Renderer intermittently hangs ("The window is not responding") and/or crashes outright.

## Behavior
Two distinct symptoms observed repeatedly with VS Code 1.129.0:

**A) Silent hang.** Both the `renderer-Management-*` and `renderer-ExtensionHost-*` sockets report success in `renderer.log` (e.g. "Creating a socket (...) was successful after N ms"), extensions activate (`Eager extensions activated` in exthost.log), and then everything goes silent — no further log output in renderer.log/exthost.log/network.log for 5+ minutes, no errors, no warnings, until the window is manually closed/reloaded. During the hang, the renderer process is *not* idle — it stays pinned at 80–90% CPU the entire time (confirmed via `ps`), which points to a busy-loop rather than a network/IPC wait.

This was reproduced identically against **three independently fresh server-side instances** (killed and let VS Code respawn `server-main.js`/`ptyHost` completely fresh each time) — remote/container side confirmed clean each time (listening socket clean, no backlog, no retransmits, extension host idling normally in `epoll_wait`, no stale locks/sockets). So the hang is client-side.

**B) Outright renderer crash.** `main.log` logs `CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 132)`, with a matching Crashpad `.dmp`. Parsing the minidump directly (no debug symbols available, so this used manual struct-offset parsing of the Crashpad minidump streams):
- `ExceptionCode = 5` (SIGTRAP), `ExceptionAddress = 0x0`, 0 exception parameters — consistent with an internal `CHECK()`/assertion trap rather than memory corruption.
- Faulting `RIP` resolves to inside `/usr/share/code/code` itself (offset `0x8c388f8` from its load base), not any extension, driver, or GPU library.

Other crash dumps from the same day showed SIGSEGV and SIGBUS as well, all inside the main `code` binary.

## Things ruled out
- SSH tunnel/keepalives: healthy throughout (checked `ssh -G`, 0 restarts on the autossh tunnel).
- WiFi power-save, suspend/resume, VPN: not involved.
- Remote container/server: confirmed clean 3x independently as above.
- GPU/hardware acceleration: still reproduces identically with `"disable-hardware-acceleration": true` in `argv.json` (ruled out a Mesa/driver correlation).
- OOM: `free -h` showed 17GB+ free, no OOM kills in `dmesg`/`journalctl`.
- Stale/leftover local processes: checked for zombies, deleted-binary handles, stale SSH control sockets — none present.

## Root cause narrowed down
Checked `/var/log/apt/history.log`: VS Code was upgraded `1.128.1-1784039518` → `1.129.0-1784074987` at a specific timestamp, and **every crash dump from that day occurred after that upgrade, none before it**. Downgrading back to 1.128.1 and holding the package (`apt-mark hold`) has fully resolved the issue — multiple clean attaches since, no hangs, no crashes.

This looks like the same failure class as #314075 (deterministic SIGTRAP / V8 `CHECK()` failure regression introduced in a single point release, fixed by downgrading exactly one version) — just recurring in a later release and with a different trigger path (Dev Containers attach instead of extension host activation).

title: BUG: Can't open model picker in Copilot Chat with delegate session "Local"

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.129.0
- OS Version: Windows 10 Pro (Build 19045)

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Install GitHub Copilot extension
2. Open Copilot Chat
3. Use "Delegate Session" with target set to "Local"
4. Click the model picker dropdown in the chat input
5. See error: `TypeError: i.charAt is not a function` in console

**Expected behavior**:

- Model picker should show available models without crashing, gracefully handling non-string metadata values from any provider.

**Root Cause**:

`getPriceCategoryLabel` in [modelPickerUtils.ts#L17](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f38816eb094a5ad5372dd54ffcd38a9c7c235330/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerUtils.ts#L17) calls `priceCategory.charAt(0)` in the `default` switch case without a type guard.

When an extension provides a non-string `priceCategory` value (e.g. GitHub Copilot with delegate session "Local"), `.charAt()` doesn't exist and throws.

```ts
export function getPriceCategoryLabel(priceCategory: string | undefined): string | undefined {
    switch (priceCategory) {
        case undefined:
        case '':
            return undefined;
        case 'low':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.low', "Low cost");
        case 'medium':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.medium', "Medium cost");
        case 'high':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.high', "High cost");
        case 'very_high':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.veryHigh', "Very high cost");
        default:
            // ⚠️ BUG: priceCategory.charAt(0) crashes when priceCategory is not a string
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.unknown', "{0} cost", priceCategory.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + priceCategory.slice(1));
    }
}
```

**Suggested fix**:

Add a `typeof` guard before calling `.charAt()` in the default case:

```ts
export function getPriceCategoryLabel(priceCategory: string | undefined): string | undefined {
    switch (priceCategory) {
        case undefined:
        case '':
            return undefined;
        case 'low':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.low', "Low cost");
        case 'medium':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.medium', "Medium cost");
        case 'high':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.high', "High cost");
        case 'very_high':
            return localize('chat.priceCategory.veryHigh', "Very high cost");
        default:
            return typeof priceCategory === 'string'
                ? localize('chat.priceCategory.unknown', "{0} cost", priceCategory.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + priceCategory.slice(1))
                : undefined;
    }
}
```

**Note**:

the sibling function `getCategoryLabel` in [modelPickerHover.ts#L215](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f38816eb094a5ad5372dd54ffcd38a9c7c235330/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerHover.ts#L215) had the same bug and was already fixed on `main` with the same `typeof` guard pattern.

title: [accessibility] [regression]: screen reader cannot announce results while navigating between results in search box

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
- VS Code Version: 1.129.0 (system setup)
- OS Version: windows 11 pro & enterprise

Steps to Reproduce:

1. NVDA is opened.
2. A project is opened with VSCode.
3. Search box is opened with CTRL + Shift + F and a text known to be in the project is entered into the search box.
4. To reach results, tab is pressed until the treeview showing results is reached.
5. When we focus on the treeview, NVDA tells us, for example: 48 results in 4 files - Search: foot
6. {regression} User navigates between results with arrow keys but NVDA cannot announce the search results, moreover even in object navigation (NVDA + num4/num6 etc.) these cannot be captured by NVDA.
  NOTE: navigation works correctly but NVDA seems unable to access the objects here.

findings:

This issue is exactly the same as issue [#320098](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320098) but there are some nuanced differences:

1. Perform searches that can yield too many results in the project, for example search for `import` in a TS project, for example 2000 result.
   - You will see that the results cannot be inspected.
2. Perform a search that may find few results in the project, for example the result count might be around 4-10.
   - You will see that the result treeview works extremely inconsistently with screen readers, with some results accessible while others are inaccessible.

***

Team,

please add accessibility tests to the VS Code test suites.
i am tired of things breaking with every update and this happening in an ever-increasing manner.  
my workflow depends on VS Code and when this tool breaks i become unable to work.
